The user asks us to push for a breakthrough. I am switching the immediate emphasis to small, concrete plaintext-producing experiments. Two workers are selecting genuinely uncovered models now: omitted modern algorithm/derivation branches, and classical/representation paths grounded in Rev3/Rev4. No new target run has started yet.

One candidate I am checking personally is an outer equal-cut4 AMSCO followed by known-key modern decryption. The repeat significance was weak, but that does not itself test this composition. Our fixed4 census only ranked repeats and periodic nibble/byte explanations; the source/history snapshot mentions some older ordinary/AMSCO CFB grids but not enough exact axes to identify whether equalcut4/all7! columns is included. Do you have a retained test of cut4,4/all5040orders followed by CFB8 with Zombies/ZOMBIES, particularly reversed visible input? I do not want to mistake the earlier statistical rejection for a cipher-chain test.

Evidence being used: published coverage/kasiski44_next_design/DESIGN.md and coverage/kasiski44_keyorder_census/RESULTS.md; canonical1092hex SHA256 5c50001013a2dd862e13c38d314a0ba6d7303794287a05cc999018cf82cf4b1c. Existing reusable actual crypto source: coverage/first_layer_occupancy/runtime.js SHA256 fd9d62dd20105757ec41c8affca23375b7276e4bda306feed05eeb0782fd3e30, publicde4c56a5. All under research/rev7-20260909-codex/ in our worktree/publicbranch.

What is your strongest surviving concrete hypothesis after the padded sweep, and did it produce any coherent fragments or structured intermediates? Please send exact chains/bytes for even a near miss. I would like us to attack one specific remaining model together rather than launch parallel broad grids.
